title: In 4,280 CRISPRi-tested human elements, validated enhancers were conserved in mammals more often if their target gene was dosage sensitive; DNase breadth predicted conservation more than function
abstract: Human enhancers that CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) screens showed to control a gene were conserved across mammals more often when that gene is sensitive to a change in its dose. This matters because the dispute about how much non-coding DNA is functional depends on whether activity measured in cells predicts natural selection. We used 4,280 enhancer-like elements that public CRISPRi screens tested in five human cell types: 545 decreased the expression of a gene and 3,735 did not. Constraint was the percentage of bases with a 240-mammal phyloP score of 2.27 or more (phyloP measures evolution slower than neutral), with exons removed. Validated enhancers had 6.6% constrained bases, CRISPRi-negative elements 5.8%, and random windows near the elements 2.4%. After adjustment for chromatin, distance, length, GC and screen, the difference was 1.2 points, and 1.8 points when DHS breadth was also adjusted. The number of 733 DNase-seq samples in which an element is open explained much more of the variance in constraint than CRISPRi function (R-squared increase 0.029 vs 0.001). Among validated enhancers, constraint increased with s_het, an estimate of the fitness cost of losing one copy of the target gene (Spearman 0.28 over 538 elements, p = 2e-11; 0.31 over 347 genes). At least 70% (95% CI 56-81%) of enhancers of genes with s_het above 0.1 had more constraint than random windows near them, against at least 39% (22-55%) for s_het of 0.01 or less. The target gene s_het still predicted constraint when the s_het of the nearest gene was in the model. Elements near a dosage-sensitive gene that they did not regulate also showed part of this trend; after distance matching, the extra slope for regulating elements fell to 55-83% of its first value (p = 0.02 to 0.10). The measured effect size added little, so the data cannot separate linear and quadratic fitness models or count unconstrained enhancers. Natural deletions in 63,046 gnomAD genomes covered validated enhancers 27% less often than CRISPRi-negative elements (p = 0.02; not significant far from promoters); this did not depend on s_het. The 1-kb human population score Gnocchi did not separate the groups. Limits: 88% of validated enhancers were tested in K562 cells; CRISPRi silences about 1 kb; s_het is a gene-level estimate. Prediction: at equal expression effect, deletion of enhancers of high-s_het genes will give larger organismal phenotypes than deletion of enhancers of low-s_het genes.

display.caption: A: Percentage of bases constrained in 240 mammals (phyloP >= 2.27, exons removed) for CRISPRi-tested element-gene pairs closer than 100 kb, by quintile of the tested gene dosage sensitivity (s_het). Blue: the element decreased the gene expression (456 pairs). Orange: the element did not change the gene (1,428 pairs). Bars are 95% bootstrap intervals over 2-Mb loci. Constraint rises with s_het for regulating pairs; for non-regulating pairs it rises over the first four quintiles and falls in the top one (interaction p = 0.02 to 0.03 for pairs < 100 kb, with or without DHS breadth). B: Likelihood profile of the exponent k in the selection index s_het x e^k (e = CRISPRi effect size) for 538 validated enhancers. The profile assumes independent elements; the locus bootstrap interval for k is 0 to 1.9, so effect size adds little beyond s_het.

A: Mammalian constraint of random local windows, CRISPRi-negative and CRISPRi-positive enhancer-like elements (95% bootstrap intervals over 2-Mb loci). B: gnomAD observed/expected variant ratio (Gnocchi, 1-kb windows); no group difference. C: Constraint against the number of 733 DNase-seq samples in which the element is open; breadth explains much more of the constraint than the CRISPRi result.

A: Natural deletions (gnomAD-SV v4.1, 50 bp to 50 kb, no exon) that cover at least half of the element, per element. Validated enhancers are covered 27% less often than CRISPRi-negative elements after adjustment for local deletion rate (p = 0.02; p = 0.13 for elements more than 10 kb from a TSS). B: Percentage of those deletions that are singletons in 63,046 genomes.
